materials.note: ELEMENT-1 BUILD-LAYER palette, owner-signed 2026-07-16 (D1/D2/D4/D6 — see element1-oak-signature-wall_DD-2026-07-16.md). Anti mono-timber: LIGHT oak on the feature walls + millwork (30% secondary); COOL plaster walls as the 60% ground (Albers D1-A: a warm wall washes the oak out); satin brass hang-rail as the 10% accent (auto-routed to the open-wardrobe rail parts) + cool microcement drawer fronts / dressing-tower back (D6-A, auto-routed to the open-wardrobe front/back parts). SUPERSEDES the proof render's warm_white_paint + birch_veneer stand-ins now that build_room renders the open:true joinery + the 40/20 slat rhythm (2026-07-16 build layer).

eye_camera.note: ELEMENT-1 hero framing (2026-07-16 build layer): stand SW in the sleeping-area free floor, look NE at the corner where the BF14 slat headboard (east) meets the BF09-3 open dressing wall (north). The bed (600 mm) sits in the foreground below the 1.15 m lens; the slat rhythm + open joinery rise behind it. Hand-placed override — validated by camera_config._spot_is_clear like the auto grid. Nudge after LOOK.

light_warm_note: ELEMENT-1 (D1-A cool-ground): a 3000 K warm-WHITE ceiling CCT, not the default 2400 K amber (1.0,0.82,0.60). The first build render proved the amber floods the enclosed oak room orange and drowns the cool-plaster ground the Albers lever depends on (LOOK 2026-07-16). Warm oak reads warm because the OAK is warm, not because the light is orange.
